chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Mattil, from Muhammad ibn 'from Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Mihran, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, who said:

I heard Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) say: Whoever is unable to connect with us, let him connect with our righteous followers; the reward for connecting with us is registered for him. And whoever is unable to perform Ziyarah (visitation) to us, let him perform Ziyarah to our righteous followers; the reward for our Ziyarah is registered for him.

key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation (specifically of the Imams or their shrines/followers)
key_terms.صِلَة: Connection or maintaining ties (with the Imams or their followers)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the righteous followers of the Imams if one cannot visit the Imams directly?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Rida (a.s.) establishing a theological principle of vicarious merit, where maintaining ties with the righteous followers (Mawali) serves as a valid substitute for direct physical proximity to the Imam. This hadith underscores the Shia concept of the 'chain of authority' and spiritual connectivity, affirming that loyalty to the Imams' community preserves the believer's share in their intercession and reward even when geographical or circumstantial barriers exist.
